GNSS observations from the CM01 receiver are analyzed to characterize temporal variations in TEC during selected geomagnetic storm events and background quiet periods.

The analysis focuses on storm-time TEC enhancements and depletions, disturbance structures, and increased ionospheric irregularities, with particular attention to phenomena such as Equatorial Plasma Bubbles (EPBs).
Comparisons between disturbed and quiet conditions are conducted to isolate storm-driven ionospheric responses from background variability.

The results provide insight into the sensitivity of low-latitude ionospheric electron density to geomagnetic forcing and highlight distinct differences between storm-time and quiet-time ionospheric behavior over Thailand.

This study contributes to improved understanding of ionospheric variability in the Southeast Asian sector and supports the development of regional ionospheric monitoring and forecasting capabilities relevant to GNSS-based navigation and communication systems.
Acknowledgments This work is financially supported by the NSRF via the Program Management Unit for the Human Resources and Institutional Development, Research and Innovation (Grant no. B41G690022).

title: Performance of Low-Cost GNSS Receivers for Storm-Time Ionospheric Monitoring

sentences.text: This study evaluates the capability of low-cost multi-frequency GNSS receivers, in conjunction with geodetic-grade instruments, to monitor storm-time ionospheric variability over the Indian region.
Emphasis is placed on both receiver performance assessment and the characterization of space-weather-driven ionospheric disturbances.

Variations in Total Electron Content (TEC) and the Rate of TEC Index (ROTI) during the extreme May 2024 superstorm (Dst ≍ −412 nT) are analysed using observations from a low-cost GNSS receiver installed at Sangli (16.52°N, 74.34°E) and co-located International GNSS Service (IGS) Hyderabad (17.42°N, 78.55°E) stations.

TEC estimates obtained from the low-cost receiver show excellent agreement with geodetic-grade IGS stations observations, with correlation coefficients exceeding 0.9, demonstrating robust performance even under severely disturbed geomagnetic conditions.

The May 2024 superstorm produced pronounced and widespread TEC depletion over low latitudes, primarily associated with dominant westward prompt-penetration electric fields and suppressed upward E×B drift.
In contrast, short-lived TEC enhancements were observed in response to X-class solar flares.
The timing and magnitude of post-flare TEC responses during the May 2024 superstorm and the November 2025 event (Dst ≍ −217 nT) are also examined.

Overall, the results confirm that low-cost multi-frequency GNSS receivers provide reliable TEC and ROTI measurements during extreme space-weather events, highlighting their strong potential for continuous storm-time ionospheric monitoring and space-weather applications in low-latitude regions.
Keywords: Low-cost GNSS receiver; Total Electron Content (TEC); Geomagnetic storms; Ionospheric variability; ROTI; Space weather

title: Monitoring Ionospheric Changes on Horseshoe Island, Antarctica: A Case Study of the May 12, 2021 Geomagnetic Storm

sentences.text: The high-latitude ionosphere is one of the most susceptible regions to energetic particle precipitation resulting from solar activities and geomagnetic storms, primarily due to open magnetic field lines.
This vulnerability renders every study conducted in the region both critical and characteristic.

In this context, ionospheric variations over the polar region are systematically monitored using data from the TUR1 GNSS station, operated within the Turkish Scientific Research Camp located on Horseshoe Island, Antarctica.
This study focuses on the geomagnetic activity event recorded on May 12, 2021 (DOY 132), during the ascending phase of the onset of Solar Cycle 25.

Within the scope of the study, Total Electron Content (TEC) estimations were performed using high-resolution RINEX observation data obtained from the TUR1 station, and ROTI (Rate of TEC Index) values—a key indicator of ionospheric irregularities were calculated.

Through the analysis of the DOY 132 case, electron density fluctuations occurring in the ionospheric F layer due to the geomagnetic storm and the impact of these fluctuations on GNSS signal quality were investigated.
Furthermore, the hardware performance and signal tracking sensitivity of the TUR1 station were evaluated based on the variations in the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) recorded during the storm.
The results demonstrate that on DOY 132, when the Kp index reached 4+, significant increases and abrupt fluctuations in TEC values were observed compared to quiet days.

These findings confirm that the TUR1 station clearly captured the increase in local ionospheric electron density (positive ionospheric storm effect) at the onset of the geomagnetic disturbance and possesses sufficient sensitivity to detect micro-scale ionospheric turbulence.

Consequently, it has been verified that the data provided by the TUR1 station constitutes a reliable, sustainable, and scientifically high-quality resource for space weather monitoring activities in the region.
"This study was supported by projects numbered "124G057" and "118Y322" within the scope of TÜBİTAK Kutup (Polar) 1001 program."
The authors thanks TUBITAK for their support.
Keywords:
Ionosphere, Total Electron Content (TEC), Geomagnetic Storm, GNSS

title: Advancing Regional Prediction of Ionospheric Variability over Chile using SUPIM-INPE under Space Weather Forcing

sentences.text: Predicting middle and upper atmosphere variability at low and mid latitudes remains challenging due to the complex coupling between solar radiation, magnetospheric forcing, and electrodynamic processes.
The South American sector exhibits strong longitudinal asymmetries and geomagnetic variability, requiring regionally evaluated predictive tools.
We use the physics-based SUPIM-INPE ionospheric model to investigate the predictive response of the ionosphere over Chile under different external drivers.
Previous applications during solar eclipse conditions demonstrated the model's capability to reproduce transient E- and F-region responses.
Building on this framework, we extend the analysis to quiet and geomagnetically disturbed conditions to assess model performance under varying levels of space weather forcing.
Model outputs of total electron content (TEC) and E- and F-region peak parameters are compared with independent observations from ground-based GNSS receivers and ionosondes across Chile.
This study strengthens regional ionospheric prediction capabilities in the South American sector and provides a scientific basis for operational implementation.
The developed framework will contribute to the Chilean Space Weather Platform currently under construction.

title: Ionospheric Response to the 17 March 2015 Geomagnetic Storm over Rabat (Morocco) Using GNSS-Derived TEC

sentences.text: We investigate the ionospheric response to the geomagnetic storm of 17 March 2015 using Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) total electron content (TEC) measurements from the International GNSS Service (IGS) station RABT located in Rabat, Morocco (34^∘N, 7^∘W).
This storm, which reached a minimum SYM-H index of $−233 nT was the most intense geomagnetic event of solar cycle 24.
Vertical TEC (VTEC) was derived from dual-frequency pseudorange observations using a single-layer ionospheric mapping function with an assumed shell height of 350 km.

A consistent preprocessing strategy was applied, including satellite- and receiver-specific Differential Code Bias (DCB) corrections, and a minimum elevation cutoff of 30^∘ to mitigate multipath and mapping errors.

The results reveal a pronounced ionospheric enhancement during the storm main phase, with ∆VTEC reaching a maximum of 45.78 TECU on 17 March, corresponding to a 158% increase relative to the quiet-day baseline value of 28.92 ± 12.91 TECU.

Correlation analysis indicates the strongest relationship between Kp and ∆VTEC at a lag of approximately three hours (r= 0.53 during storm periods), suggesting a delayed ionospheric response to geomagnetic forcing.

These results contribute to a better understanding of mid-latitude ionospheric dynamics during extreme space-weather events and highlight the potential impacts on GNSS-based positioning and navigation systems in the European─African sector.

title: Freshly Generated Super Sunrise Plasma Bubbles During the Geomagnetic Storm on November 5-6, 2023

sentences.text: During the geomagnetic storm on November 5-6, 2023, freshly generated super sunrise equatorial plasma bubbles (EPBs) and associated irregularities over the 80-140°E sector were observed combining ground-based and space observations from GNSS, ionosondes, HF Doppler records, and several satellite missions (COSMIC2, Swarm, and DMSP).
The morphology and evolutionary characteristics of the super sunrise EPBs were revealed, showing their potential strong westward drift and related conjugate features.
The in-situ plasma depletion structures at mid-latitudes could persist into the afternoon, lasting approximately 10 hours.
Meanwhile, mid-latitude stations recorded rare strong scintillation triggered by sunrise plasma bubbles.
Intense range spread F and significant pre-sunrise ionospheric uplift were observed by different ionosonde stations.
The generation of super sunrise EPBs may have been driven by a combined effect of overshielding electric fields, disturbance dynamo electric field, and enhanced equatorward winds.
Finally, a comparative analysis of the characteristics and dominant mechanisms of freshly generated sunrise EPB events was conducted.

The formation of super sunrise EPBs is more closely dependent on storm-time enhanced equatorward winds and the potential seeding role of large-scale wavelike structure (LSWS), while also showing some connections to post-sunset EPBs.

title: Observational and Numerical Study of Ionospheric Responses to Traveling Atmospheric Disturbances and Neutral Wind Shear During the November 2025 Geomagnetic Storm

sentences.text: The ionosphere─thermosphere system can undergo severe disturbances during geomagnetic storms, leading to significant impacts on satellite communication, navigation, and orbital drag.
These disturbances can manifest as either enhancements or depletions in ionospheric electron density.

Here we report an abnormal electron density enhancement during the November 2025 geomagnetic storm, coincident with unusually strong poleward meridional winds, using the observations from Incoherent Scatter Radar over Sanya and Beidou geostationary satellites.
The shear of the meridional wind associated with gravity waves induced by the storm, played a dominant role in the changes of ionospheric electron density, as reproduced by the numerical model.

title: Propagation features of LSTIDs originated by minor CIR / HSS-driven magnetic storm under solar terminator conditions

sentences.text: Geomagnetic storms are primary drivers of large-scale variability in the geospace.
They can efficiently generate atmospheric gravity waves (AGWs) through intense energy deposition, primarily via Joule heating, Lorentz forcing, and particle precipitation.
Large-scale traveling ionospheric disturbances (LSTIDs) represent the ionospheric manifestations of AGWs launched from auroral regions.

Corotating interaction region (CIR) / high-speed stream (HSS)─driven storms, although generally classified as minor to moderate based on peak geomagnetic indices, are characterized by their recurrent nature and prolonged duration.

This enables CIR / HSS events to deposit a cumulative amount of energy into the upper atmosphere that can be comparable to or even exceed that of moderate interplanetary coronal mass ejection─driven storms.
As a result, CIR / HSS─driven disturbances are particularly effective in generating persistent and continuously fluctuating wave activity.
The propagation characteristics of LSTIDs, such as velocity, direction, and damping rate, depend strongly on the background state of the thermosphere and ionosphere.
Thermospheric winds act as an efficient directional filter, capable of both facilitating and suppressing wave propagation.
In addition, as AGWs and LSTIDs propagate, they lose energy through viscosity, thermal conductivity, and ion drag.
The solar terminator (ST) also represents a repeatable and well-regulated source of forcing that fundamentally modifies LSTID propagation conditions.
The motion of the ST produces abrupt changes in solar radiation absorption, generating strong horizontal gradients in thermospheric temperature, pressure and wind.

These gradients act as an additional source of AGWs and LSTIDs, which often introduce pronounced zonal propagation components that differ from the predominantly equatorward propagation of storm-induced LSTIDs.

We analyzed the LSTID characteristics over Europe during a CIR / HSS─driven magnetic storm that occurred from 30 March to 6 April 2023, using data acquired from three European ionosondes (Juliusruh, Dourbes, and Pruhonice) and a dense network of the European GNSS receivers.

A unified methodology incorporating 180-min trend fitting, spectral and cross-correlation analyses, and 30 ─ 120-min band-pass filtering was applied to detect and characterize LSTIDs using temporal variations of the F2-layer peak electron density (NmF2) and spatio-temporal variations of detrended total electron content (dTEC).

For this magnetic storm period, we found that ST conditions at sunset were most favorable for the propagation of storm-driven LSTIDs to middle and even low-to-middle latitudes without significant attenuation.
A comparison of dominant LSTID periods and phase velocities revealed good consistency between ionosonde and GNSS results at nearby locations.
An increase in the dominant LSTID periods from 75 to 90 minutes was observed as the disturbances propagated farther southward.
Clear differences in LSTID characteristics were identified between regions involved in the analysis before and after the ST sunset passage at altitudes between 150 ─ 350 km.
While the LSTID horizontal phase velocities maintained an overall southward direction, their values varied considerably, ranging from 300 to 800 m/s depending on the specific location.

title: Detection and analysis of traveling ionospheric disturbances at mid-latitudes over Europe using a combination of GNSS and all-sky imager observations

sentences.text: The ionosphere, a highly dynamic region of the Earth's atmosphere, is constantly shaped by solar activity.
During geomagnetic storms, ionospheric phenomena can significantly affect technological infrastructure on Earth and in near-Earth space.
Traveling ionospheric disturbances (TIDs) are one of the manifestations of this increased geomagnetic activity.
This research focuses on detecting and identifying the large- and medium-scale TIDs occurring at mid-latitudes, over the central European sector.
Since 2023, we have analyzed several events to identify the conditions under which TIDs form and their propagation characteristics.

In this study, we combine observations from a dense network of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers with simultaneous measurements collected by an all-sky imaging camera located at Zugspitze in southern Germany.
We analyze total electron content (TEC), TEC anomalies and the rate of TEC index (ROTI), comparing them to the spatial and temporal propagation of airglow emissions.
The camera records nocturnal airglow and auroral emissions at 557.7, 630.0, and 777.4 nm wavelengths, enabling the investigation of ionospheric structures at various altitudes.
Our results demonstrate a high degree of consistency between GNSS-based and optical observations.

Furthermore, all-sky imaging provides more in-depth analysis of the physical and chemical characteristics of disturbances, including their height, the emitting species responsible for the observed airglow, and the relationship between TIDs and auroral activity.
Our results obtained contributed to a better understanding of ionospheric variability and its impact on radio wave propagation and GNSS-based systems during disturbed geomagnetic conditions.
This, in turn, improved the characterization of mid-latitude TIDs.

title: Estimation of the ionization rate of the ionosphere during X-class solar flares

sentences.text: Solar flares are one of the most intense space weather events affecting the Earth's ionosphere.

Increased X-ray and ultraviolet radiation fluxes during flares lead to a sharp increase in the ionization of the neutral atmosphere and, consequently, a significant increase in the electron concentration.
The occurrence of such sudden ionospheric disturbances affects the propagation of shortwave radio waves and can cause disruptions in communication and navigation systems.
Instrumental methods for studying the state and dynamics of the ionosphere make it possible to detect the emergence of ionospheric irregularities and determine their main characteristics.
However, existing experimental data are insufficient for a comprehensive analysis of the processes occurring in various ionospheric layers during solar flares.

In this study, experimental and theoretical methods were used to assess the impact of solar flare electromagnetic radiation on the state and dynamics of the Earth's ionosphere in the altitude range of 60─600 km.

Using the empirical solar radiation model (FISM2) and the neutral atmosphere model (NRLMSISE-00) as an example for two X-class flares that occurred on September 6, 2017, vertical ionization rate profiles were calculated.

The calculated results were compared with experimental data on the total electron content of the ionosphere, obtained using a GNSS receiver located at the Mikhnevo mid-latitude geophysical observatory.

It was found that the combination of empirical models allows for a qualitative assessment of the temporal dynamics of the increase in the ionization rate, and the observed excess of calculated data over measured results may be due to the influence of recombination processes not accounted for in the calculations.
The results obtained confirm the validity of the proposed approaches and open up opportunities for further research in this area.
The research was supported by the Ministry of Science and Higher Education of the Russian Federation (project registration number 122032900175-6).

title: The Comparative Analysis of Local Dst at KMITL Chumphon and Global Dst During Intense Geomagnetic Storms in the Ascending Phase of Solar Cycle 25

sentences.text: This study investigates the relationship between the local Dst index derived from the KMITL Chumphon geomagnetic observatory in Thailand and the global Dst index provided by the World Data Center (WDC) for Geomagnetism, Kyoto, during intense geomagnetic storm events in the rising phase of Solar Cycle 25.

The local Dst index was calculated using the horizontal geomagnetic field component (H), obtained from Ground-based Fluxgate Magnetometer (GFGM) measurements sampled at 10 Hz, averaged to hourly values, and referenced to a quiet-day baseline derived from five International Quiet Days (IQDs).

A comparative analysis between local Dst and global Dst reveals that the local Dst at KMITL Chumphon exhibited a significantly deeper depression (approximately −250 nT) during the storm main phase compared to the global minimum (around −100 nT), indicating enhanced geomagnetic disturbances at low latitudes.

Pearson correlation analysis yielded a moderate positive correlation (r = 0.64) between local and global Dst, with a linear regression slope of 1.26, suggesting that local geomagnetic responses tend to be amplified relative to global averages due to regional magnetospheric and ionospheric current systems.

In addition, Total Electron Content (TEC) variations from three GNSS stations Chiang Mai (MAIG), SIET KMITL Bangkok, KMITL Chumphon, and IRI model were examined to assess ionospheric responses to geomagnetic activity.
Results show a slight TEC enhancement during the storm main phase followed by depletion and gradual recovery, demonstrating strong coupling between geomagnetic disturbances and ionospheric dynamics.
Keywords: Geomagnetic storm, Dst, TEC, Solar Cycle 25, IRI model

title: TOMIRIS: A real-time International Reference Ionosphere using slant Total Electron Content

sentences.text: The IRI is very successful as a model for representing the climatological behaviour of the global ionosphere.
It is designed to be able to capture the monthly median behaviour of the ionosphere, and includes a storm model to capture typical variability associated with geomagnetic storm conditions.
There has long been interest in augmenting the IRI using data assimilation to produce a real-time ionospheric model.
The first such model was the IRTAM model, which assimilated data from ionosondes.
Other techniques have been explored, with particular interest given to techniques using effective driving indices.
A new real-time data assimilation model based on the IRI, called TOMIRIS, has been operating at the University of Birmingham since April 4th, 2025.
TOMIRIS uses the same bottomside and near-topside formulation as the IRI, but is capable of representing finer spatial and temporal scales.
It assimilates data from the GIRO ionosondes, and slant Total Electron Content (sTEC) from over 2100 Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers worldwide.
This allows it to produce an updated ionospheric specification with less than 5 minutes latency.
It uses a particle filter, a nonlinear data assimilation technique which has been successfully used for other ionospheric models such as A-CHAIM and AIDA.
The results from the first year of TOMIRIS operation will be presented.
The current and historical output of TOMIRIS is available in real-time via an API using the AIDA interpreter package https://github.com/breid-phys/aida-ionosphere.

title: NN modelling of the topside ionosphere based on four solar cycles of measurements

sentences.text: The Earth's ionosphere affects the propagation of signals from the Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS).

The part of the ionosphere above the F2-layer peak, known as the topside ionosphere, contains a major portion of the total electron content and is therefore crucial for both scientific and practical applications.

One of the major challenges for modeling the topside ionosphere has been the sparse data coverage, primarily limited to in-situ observations along satellite orbits that are relatively fixed in time and do not provide comprehensive three-dimensional coverage.
Over the past two decades, a large number of radio occultation (RO) electron density profiles have become available, offering a valuable data source for enhancing our modeling capabilities.

In this study, we use RO, in-situ, and digisonde data, along with historical observations from topside sounder missions, to develop an updated version of the Neural Network model of Electron density in the Topside ionosphere (NET).
The updated model is based on the data set spanning approximately 4 solar cycles and therefore covers a wide range of solar activity and geomagnetic conditions.

We validate the model using data from several prominent ionospheric missions and demonstrate that it generalizes well to unseen observations, with approximately 90% of the predictions falling within a factor of two of the measurements.

We analyze the scientific capabilities of the model during geomagnetic storms, by investigating the behavior of the topside ionosphere, particularly the storm-time enhancements of the F2-peak height (hmF2) at high latitudes and their equatorward propagation as depicted by the model.
We discuss the current challenges and limitations in modeling the high latitude ionosphere and potential ways forward in order to address these challenges in the future.

title: Ionospheric TEC and Geomagnetic Field Responses to Geomagnetic Storms: Validation of IRI-2020 Model Using GPS Observations Over Chumphon, Thailand

sentences.text: This study investigates the ionospheric Total Electron Content (TEC) response and geomagnetic field components to geomagnetic storms and validates the performance of the IRI-2020 model using GPS observations over Chumphon, Thailand (KMITL Chumphon station: 10.73°N, 99.37°E, 3.77°N dip), a low latitude station influenced by equatorial electrodynamic processes.
The analysis focuses on selected geomagnetic storm periods in 2025, during the ascending phase of Solar Cycle 25, considering storm conditions classified as G3-G4 with Dst values ranging from -96
nT to -412 nT.
A three-day analysis window, covering one day before the storm, the storm day, and one day after, was applied to characterize pre-storm, main phase, and early recovery ionospheric conditions.
The Dst index was used to delineate storm phases and provide a global reference for storm intensity.

GPS TEC observations were used to validate IRI-2020 model outputs under geomagnetic storm conditions, while concurrent variations in the geomagnetic field components (X, Y, and Z) from ground-based magnetometer measurements were examined to support the interpretation of storm-time ionospheric variability.

The results indicate pronounced daytime TEC enhancements during storm main phases, typically occurring near the Dst minimum and accompanied by significant disturbances in the geomagnetic X and Z components, suggesting the influence of storm-time electrodynamic driving processes.
Nighttime geomagnetic storm periods exhibited comparatively weaker TEC responses.
The IRI-2020 model generally underestimates peak TEC values during periods of intense geomagnetic activity at this low-latitude location.

These findings provide an observational basis for validating the IRI-2020 model under disturbed geomagnetic conditions and contribute to improved understanding of low latitude ionospheric behavior during geomagnetic storms.

title: AENEAS: An Operational Data Assimilation Thermosphere Model to Support Satellite Operations

abbreviations.MOSWOC: Met Office Space Weather Operations Centre

sentences.text: Accurate specification of the coupled thermosphere─ionosphere system is essential for reliable satellite orbit determination, collision avoidance, and re-entry prediction, particularly during disturbed space weather conditions.
We present the development, operational deployment, and validation of AENEAS, an operational model within the UK Met Office Space Weather Operations Centre (MOSWOC).
AENEAS is an ensemble-based data assimilation framework designed to provide real-time specification and short-term forecasting of the upper atmosphere.

Originally developed for ionospheric electron density assimilation, the system has been extended to deliver self-consistent thermospheric mass density specification through coupled modelling and data-constrained drivers.

The operational configuration integrates multi-source observations, including GNSS-derived total electron content, ionosonde data, and space-based measurements, within an ensemble Kalman filter framework to produce dynamically consistent state estimates.
A key focus of this work is thermosphere specification and its impact on satellite orbit determination.
Neutral density variability in the thermosphere is a dominant source of uncertainty in low Earth orbit (LEO) drag modelling.

AENEAS provides enhanced density estimates during both quiet and geomagnetically disturbed conditions, reducing model bias and improving temporal responsiveness relative to empirical climatological models.
Validation has been performed against independent accelerometer-derived density datasets and through orbit propagation experiments using representative LEO satellites.
Results demonstrate measurable reductions in orbit prediction error growth rates.

Operational implementation at MOSWOC required robustification of the assimilation pipeline, automation of data ingest, fail-safe ensemble cycling, and integration with existing space weather forecasting products.
We describe the architecture of the operational system and its performance metrics.

AENEAS represents a significant step toward fully data-assimilative, operational thermosphere─ionosphere modelling in the UK, strengthening national capability in space domain awareness and satellite drag forecasting.

title: Fusion-Dst: an operational geomagnetic storm forecasting capability integrating science-driven and machine-learning approaches

sentences.text: Given the increasing debris environment in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), there is strong interest among U.S. agencies, commercial entities, and international organizations in managing hazards associated with debris collisions.

The current operational baseline for recent, current, and predicted thermospheric density is the data-assimilative model used by the U.S. Space Force (USSF), known as the High Accuracy Satellite Drag Model (HASDM).
HASDM employs the JB2008 thermospheric density model and its associated solar and geomagnetic indices (SGI) to generate forecasts out to 144 hours (6 days).
The JB2008 SGI are provided by Space Environment Technologies (SET) and include the S10, M10, Y10, and F10 solar indices, as well as the Dst and Ap geomagnetic indices.
Licata et al.
[2020] evaluated the forecast performance of these indices and found that their accuracy degrades during periods of high solar activity and geomagnetic storms.
This work presents Fusion-Dst, an operational hybrid science─machine-learning geomagnetic storm forecasting system designed to improve Dst forecasting for LEO satellite operations.

A key motivation for the development of Fusion-Dst is the performance of SET's legacy science-driven operational storm forecasting algorithm, Anemomilos, which has a relatively high false-positive rate.

This limitation arises because the interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) orientation (and associated Bz polarity governing geomagnetic coupling) within an Earth-directed CME cannot be determined until in situ measurements are available only hours prior to arrival at Earth.

As a result, accurate prediction of geomagnetic storms at lead times beyond several hours remains fundamentally challenging, while longer lead times are required to support satellite operations and conjunction assessment.

To address these limitations, Andong Hu (SWxTREC, University of Colorado) developed machine-learned (ML) algorithms that provide both a 6-hour deterministic Dst forecast and a 48-hour probabilistic Dst forecast.
These ML-based approaches demonstrate substantially improved performance relative to traditional science-driven storm forecasting techniques, including SET's legacy Anemomilos system.

Through a NASA SBIR Phase I and Phase II effort, SET has further developed, matured, and operationalized these ML-based Dst forecasting algorithms (with Hu serving as Co-Investigator), integrating them into SET's existing operational framework as a unified storm forecasting system, hereafter referred to as Fusion-Dst, which delivers forecast Dst directly to the USSF for use within HASDM.
When evaluated over the 2018-2025 period, Fusion-Dst's 6-hour deterministic ML-based Dst forecast demonstrates substantial reductions in forecast error under both quiet and storm-time conditions.

Specifically, Fusion-Dst achieves a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 7.9 nT during geomagnetically quiet conditions, compared to 18.3 nT for the legacy Anemomilos forecast, and an RMSE of 27.6 nT during storm conditions, compared to 66.4 nT for Anemomilos.
The most impactful new capability of Fusion-Dst is the introduction of a 48-hour probabilistic ML-based Dst forecast.

This probabilistic forecast provides actionable guidance within Fusion-Dst's operational framework by informing whether the deterministic Anemomilos-based storm forecast should be issued, thereby mitigating the historically high false-positive rate associated with science-driven storm prediction.
When evaluated over the 2018-2025 period, incorporation of the probabilistic forecast reduces the Anemomilos false-positive rate by 94%, while simultaneously reducing the false-negative rate by 26%.
Overall, Fusion-Dst, scheduled to become fully operational in Summer 2026, represents a substantial advancement in operational geomagnetic storm forecasting.

By significantly reducing both false-positive and false-negative storm forecasts, Fusion-Dst directly improves thermospheric density specification and prediction used in LEO satellite propagation, leading to enhanced conjunction assessment, improved satellite tracking accuracy, and more robust space object catalog maintenance.

title: Inferring Dominant Acceleration Mechanisms using the longitudinal spread of SEPs during the 28 May 2021 event

sentences.text: Solar energetic particles (SEPs) are commonly accelerated by magnetic reconnection in solar flares or by shock waves driven by coronal mass ejections (CMEs).
Especially during large events, both potential acceleration regions are present.

To infer which is the dominant acceleration mechanism for specific particle populations in a single event, we study the longitudinal distribution of particle intensities using multiple heliospheric observers.
We analyse the 28 May 2021 SEP event using well-separated observations from Solar Orbiter, Parker Solar Probe, STEREO A, and near-Earth observers: SOHO Wind.
Gaussian curves are fitted to particle intensities as a function of the observer's location at regular time intervals.
These fits are applied to 100 keV 1 MeV electrons, as well as 14 MeV 32 MeV protons, to infer the time evolution of the source longitude and the longitudinal width of the particle distribution.

Our results indicate that, for this event, the characteristics of higher-energy particle movement are consistent with acceleration by an outward-moving source, whereas 100 keV electrons display characteristics in line with those associated with flare acceleration.

Our investigation demonstrates a useful technique for inferring acceleration mechanisms in solar events, and the methodology has been developed into a publicly available tool through the SOLER project.
The SOLER project has received funding from the European Union's Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under grant agreement No 101134999.
This study reflects only the authors' view, and the European Commission is not responsible for any use that may be made of the information it contains.

title: Photonics Enabling Next Generation Magnetograph Networks

sentences.text: Space weather poses increasing risks to national security, satellite operations, power grids, aviation, and global communications, driven by solar activity such as coronal mass ejections (CMEs) and flares.
Current and planned magnetograph networks are based on expensive and bulky designs which impose limits on hemispheric coverage.

The IPSOS (Imaging Photonic Spectropolarimeter for Observing the Sun) solar magnetograph is a transformative, compact instrument that offers the possibility of re-imagining how they might be used and distributed.
In this talk, we review the current and expected future state of the IPSOS instrument and discuss its role in measuring the full vector field of the Sun at unprecedented accuracy.

The resulting observations could finally resolve questions on how the solar magnetic field is generated by the solar dynamo and the major space weather it drives: from the 22-year magnetic cycle that modulates total solar irradiance, to global coronal magnetic fields that structure the solar wind, to magnetic eruptions from sunspot active regions that power coronal mass ejections triggering major geomagnetic storms.

title: Investigating CME Parameter Sensitivity on L1 observations with the SWASTI Framework

sentences.text: Space weather forecasting has become critical in the modern technological era, where geomagnetic disturbances can significantly impact satellites, communication systems, navigation infrastructure, and power systems.
Accurate prediction of coronal mass ejection (CME) arrival time and associated plasma properties at L1 is therefore essential for reliable space weather forecasting.
In this study, we use the Space Weather Adaptive Simulation (SWASTI) framework to investigate how intrinsic CME parameters influence plasma properties at L1.
We construct an ensemble of simulations by systematically varying key CME input parameters, including initial density, velocity, and magnetic flux.
We then analyze how these parameters affect peak plasma density, velocity, magnetic field strength, and arrival time at L1.
This ensemble approach enables isolation of parameter sensitivity while preserving the physical consistency of the heliospheric evolution.
Using multi-metric sensitivity analysis and nonlinear ensemble modeling, we aim to quantify the dominant drivers and secondary contributors governing different plasma parameters at L1.
The presentation will discuss both qualitative physical interpretation and quantitative characterization of these parameter dependencies.

Through this systematic ensemble-based investigation using SWASTI, we seek to clarify how primary CME inputs control heliospheric responses and how secondary parameters contribute additional structure beyond first-order effects.
Such insights will significantly help refining predictive modeling, planning observation strategies and advancing the physical basis of space weather forecasting.

title: Bridging Causality and Forecasting in Space Weather: An Approach Integrating Information-Theoretic and NARMAX Machine Learning (IT-NARMAX-ML)

sentences.text: Accurate space weather forecasting is critical for safeguarding satellite infrastructure and terrestrial power grids from geomagnetic disturbances and radiation hazards.
While data-driven models have gained prominence, achieving a balance between high-fidelity predictive accuracy and physical interpretability remains a significant challenge.

This work presents a novel hybrid framework that bridges the gap between information-theoretic (IT) causality analysis and a sparse, interpretable machine learning (ML) model, called NARMAX (Nonlinear AutoRegressive Moveing Average with eXogenous inputs).

The proposed framework first employs IT methods to conduct rigorous nonlinear causality tests, effectively quantifying the information flow between solar wind drivers (e.g. velocity, density, pressure), the interplanetary magnetic field components, and the target magnetospheric responses.

These causal insights serve as a principled feature selection mechanism to inform the NARMX-ML process, which constructs parsimonious, mathematically explicit models that characterise the underlying system dynamics without the opacity of traditional black-box approaches.

Validated against real magnetospheric indices data, experimental results demonstrate that this hybrid approach, IT-NARMAX-ML, significantly improves both forecasting and interpretation capability over conventional ML methods.

By identifying the sparse functional structures governing Sun-Earth coupling, this work provides a robust, physically grounded tool for real-time risk mitigation and the advancement of predictive geospace science.

title: The Mystery of Helium-3 Enrichment in SEP Acceleration: Evidence from Wave-Particle Interactions, Isotopic Fractionation, and Turbulent Acceleration

sentences.text: Extremely high-energy SEPs, reaching GeV energies, accelerated during impulsive solar flares and in connection with CMEs, constitute a major driver of hazardous space weather events.

These relativistic particles pose substantial risks to spacecraft and crew safety in deep-space exploration missions and can inflict catastrophic damage on ground-based infrastructure, particularly power grids and other critical elements of the electromagnetic environment.

Spectral observations reveal that the GeV-level acceleration process in SEP events is highly complex and multi-component-abundance-isotopes, involving a diverse mix of ion species, including hydrogen (electron and proton, 73%), helium (25%, The mass-to-charge ratio for 3He is 1.5, while for 4He it is 2.0), and heavier ions.
The acceleration of SEPs to GeV energies remains a major unresolved challenge in solar physics.
The issue is particularly pronounced in 3He-rich impulsive SEP events, where the observed isotopic composition presents one of the most striking anomalies in the field.
The pre-acceleration 3He/4He abundance ratio ranges from approximately 4X10E-4 to 5X10E-4.

In contrast, post-acceleration measurements in these impulsive events frequently reveal ratios approaching or exceeding unity (>1), corresponding to enrichment factors of up to 10E5 times relative to the ambient solar composition.

This extraordinary isotopic fractionation—first identified in the early 1960s—has remained one of the most persistent and compelling enigmas in the physics of particle acceleration for more than six decades.
In this study, we investigate the acceleration and 3He enrichment processes in SEP events using a statistical plasma-physics framework combined with turbulence-filtering theory.
Our approach explicitly incorporates the realistic proton-to-electron mass ratio, the mass-to-charge ratios of the relevant ion species, and turbulence resistivity and viscosity terms.

This is achieved within a fully coupled hydrodynamics─magnetohydrodynamics─kinetic framework that spans continuous spatial and temporal scales—avoiding the conventional separation into independent micro-kinetic and macro-dynamic regimes.
Simulations are performed on a supercomputer using our newly developed relativistic hybrid particle-in-cell lattice-Boltzmann method (RHPIC-LBM) code.
This innovative numerical approach enables fully self-consistent modeling of the multi-scale, multiphase processes that drive the extreme enhancements of Helium-3 observed in impulsive solar SEPs.

Our simulations demonstrate that high-frequency magnetic fluctuations at kinetic scales play a crucial role in driving the self-organized organization of perturbations, while plasma fluctuations sustain these waves.
When the frequency of these perturbations approaches the Langmuir oscillation frequency, resonant wave-particle interactions become highly effective.
Langmuir turbulence acceleration, driven by nonlinear resonant wave-particle interactions, preferentially accelerates particles whose resonance conditions align with those of ³He.

This selective resonance renders the acceleration of Helium-3 far more efficient than that of Helium-4, providing a key mechanism to explain the extreme Helium-3 enrichment observed in impulsive SEP events.
